title: A protocol to evaluate immunoglobulin deposits in mouse glomeruli
protocol: Euthanize mice by carbon dioxide asphyxiation.
Place the mice in an euthanasia chamber.
Displace air inside the chamber with 100% CO2 for about a minute to induce loss of consciousness.
Increase the flow rate of CO2 to 100% for two minutes to stop respiration.
Maintain the CO2 flow for at least one to two minutes after respiratory arrest.
Absorb CO2 from the chamber for two minutes post-respiratory arrest.
Place euthanized mouse in a supine position on a disinfected dissection platform.
Isolate mouse kidneys for preservation.
Pin the legs of the mouse at a 90° angle to the body on the dissection board.
Spray ethanol on the ventral side of the mouse.
Use dissection scissors to make a midline incision pointing towards the tail to cut open the skin.
Make lateral incisions at the shoulder joints and the pelvic girdles to peel open the skin easily.
Use forceps and fingers to carefully separate skin layers while keeping internal organs intact.
Cut open the abdominal membrane with dissection scissors to expose internal organs.
Locate the kidneys, then gently separate them from associated tissue using clean tweezers and dissection scissors.
Cut the renal artery, vein, and ureter to liberate the kidneys.
Transfer the kidneys to a 1.5 mL eppendorf tube containing 1× PBS or RPMI-1640 media.
Gently fill the corners of the cryomold with OCT compound making sure it is present evenly throughout the mold.
Ensure no introduction of bubbles in the OCT compound.
Fill a steel can halfway with 100% acetone and rest it on dry ice for a minute.
Add one or two small chips of dry ice at a time to the acetone to lower the temperature.
Take the isolated kidney and cut lengthwise with a scalpel or dissection scissors.
Place the desired section of the tissue in the center of the OCT compound on the cryomold with the incision surface face down.
Dispense more OCT onto the tissue specimen until it is completely covered.
Allow the OCT to settle for 15–30 seconds.
Remove any air bubbles that form before proceeding.
Dip the cryomold containing the tissue and OCT compound into chilled acetone using long forceps.
Freeze the contents of the cryomold by turning them completely white (opaque) within 2 minutes.
Remove the tissue block from the cryomold and trim the edges with a razor blade.
Place the OCT-embedded tissue in pre-cooled cryovials or tissue cassettes.
Store the OCT-embedded tissue at -80°C.
Transfer the specimen tissue block to the cryostat chamber.
Let the tissue block equilibrate to the set temperature of the cryostat.
Mount the tissue block onto the tissue block holder of the cryostat with OCT.
Align the tissue block with the correct orientation of the specimen.
Choose the desired thickness (7 μm) of the sections.
Turn the cryostat handwheel to form a strip or ribbon of sections of the desired thickness.
Transfer the sections onto a clean pre-chilled microscope slide.
Rub the back of the slide with the hand to warm it to ensure the sections adhere well.
Air-dry the slides at room temperature (21°C) for 20–30 min to ensure the tissue section adheres more strongly to the slide.
Place the air-dried slides in a slide box wrapped in foil and placed inside a zip-top bag.
Store the packaged slides at −80°C.
Remove OCT embedded tissue slides stored at −80°C and thaw at room temperature (21°C).
Dry the sides of the slides with a lint-free tissue.
Arrange the slides in an appropriate slide staining jar for rehydration.
Wash the slides in Phosphate Buffered Saline (PBS) (wash buffer) for 5 min (3 times), changing the solution between each wash.
Mark out a boundary encircling but a few millimeters away from the tissue using a mini PAP pen.
Leave to rest for 1–2 minutes for the wax to completely dry.
Add (∼300 μL) blocking buffer (3% Bovine Serum Albumin (BSA)/0.1% Triton X-100 in PBS) to the slides to prevent non-specific binding of antibodies.
Incubate at room temperature (21°C) for 1-2 hours on a rocker in a humidified chamber.
Remove the blocking buffer and add the appropriate dilution of the primary antibody in PBS.
Incubate the slides at 4°C overnight (18–20 hours).
Wash the slides in PBS for 5 minutes (thrice) at room temperature (21°C).
Add appropriate dilutions of secondary antibody labeled with the fluorochrome in 5% BSA/PBS, if primary antibody is unconjugated.
Incubate at room temperature (21°C) for 1-2 hours, if primary antibody is unconjugated.
Rinse the slides in PBS for 5 minutes (thrice), if primary antibody is unconjugated.
Wipe off excess PBS on the slide without disrupting the tissue.
Apply mounting medium (ProLong™ Gold Antifade Mountant) directly to the tissue.
Place a coverslip on top of the tissue using forceps carefully.
Remove any air bubbles from under the coverslip.
Allow the mounting medium to set at room temperature (21°C) for 15-30 minutes.
Store dried slides at 4°C for imaging.
Switch mercury lamp on at least 10 min earlier to warm up for imaging.
Apply a small drop of immersion oil onto the slide or objective and place the slide face down onto the objective.
Focus on several glomeruli per slide section and capture images.
Save images as high-resolution TIFF files.
Weigh the mouse.
Calculate the amount of immunoglobulin dose according to the weight of the mouse.
Use a mechanical restraint device to restrain the mouse.
Disinfect the tail with 75% ethanol.
Adjust the position of the tail’s lateral side and secure it with the left hand.
Insert the catheter needle at a 30° angle into the vein, 2 cm from the tip of the tail.
Inject the immunoglobulin solution slowly and steadily.
Carefully remove the needle once the contents have been injected.
Apply gentle pressure to the injection site until bleeding stops.
Release the mouse out of the restraint device.
Check for vital signs in the mouse.
Place the mouse back in the original cage immediately after injection.
